geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant cantilever into a split-wing mass so the public edge can be opened while preserving a single dominant program volume.
Split laterally across the plan to create a clear void aligned with the frontage response.
Retain continuity across the split so the form remains one architecture rather than two isolated blocks.
Add a ground-spine response to keep the public threshold legible at grade.
Tune the split to produce a usable public void rather than a decorative seam.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the cantilever-only dominant mass with a split-wing logic so the street edge can open toward the verified access side instead of remaining sealed.
Use the split axis to open the mass laterally and make a public threshold along the frontage side.
Keep a connective bridge so the dominant gesture remains one continuous mass rather than two unrelated fragments.
Ensure the split mass preserves a grounded public spine rather than floating apart.
Create a legible void proportion suitable for an entry court or public seam without over-fragmenting the mass.

rationale: The candidate is a compact stepped/cantilevered mass that is at least coherent across views, so it avoids total fragmentation or view-only legibility. However, the visible form reads more like a generic clipped object with an upper overhang than a neighborhood-living mass with a strong public threshold. The blue access edge is not answered by a legible court, notch, or undercut; the ground is mostly sealed. The silhouette has some continuity, but the stepped/cantilevered moves are not yet program-meaningful and do not establish a clear public void or active street edge. Because the program brief requires a compact street building with one clear public void or terrace and an active ground edge, the current mass does not satisfy program_fit_hard_pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller, tower-like profile and more vertical emphasis than a compact neighborhood-living street building; do not copy the height strategy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered overall silhouette can read as a coherent public-facing mixed-use mass when the section remains continuous.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office atrium typology may overstate inward corporate identity; adapt only the void-and-hierarchy principle, not the tower podium language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear carved central void can organize a compact mass and strengthen public threshold logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a flatter single-story object; the candidate needs a more convincing active ground and void, not just a stepped roof.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low, legible ground contact with a distinct public edge/canopy can support neighborhood-facing commercial use.

warnings: Parcel containment and view coherence appear acceptable, but the access edge response is weak.
The dominant gesture is readable, but it does not yet produce a convincing public void or entry seam.
Do not read the stepped roof as sufficient program section; it lacks a clear ground/public relation.
